rows.en:
Because she was wearing something like a white Noh mask, you see.
You couldn't even read her expression.
The five stuck to the ceiling had been nailed up through various parts of their bodies with five-inch spikes.
And the masked woman was clinging there, leaning her weight on their corpses.
He was struck speechless.
He couldn't even scream. He was transfixed by the eerie world that filled his vision.
That became his last memory.
Because the very next instant, the masked woman came skittering across the ceiling like a spider and was on him.
...And at that moment, he wondered.{p}
What were those small black creatures that had been carrying those three away...?{p}

It didn't matter one bit to him, since he was about to die.
Maybe people think about pretty silly things right before they die.{p}

...So what became of those six, you ask?
...They were never found.
The next day, the teacher who'd gone home and left them in the make-up class and the teacher who'd been asked to take over both searched the old school building before the problem could get any bigger.
But they didn't find their bodies, or even a single drop of blood.
And those two teachers got their stories straight: they said they'd sent the students home properly.
Awful, isn't it?
And so the six were listed as missing.
In the end, no one ever saw any of them again.
Still, their classmates knew the six who vanished had stayed behind at school for a make-up class.
And since they disappeared right after that, strange rumors started going around.{p}

All kinds of weird rumors spread, too: that strange groans could be heard from the girls' restroom on the third floor of the old school building, or that someone had seen the missing students there.
So people started saying it was Hanako-san's curse.
That Hanako-san had taken the six of them away.
Whether those six wandered into another world, or whether it really was Hanako-san's curse, nobody knows.
...And that's the end of the story about the old school building.
Of course, nobody actually saw the six of them being killed, so it isn't very credible, is it?{p}

But I just can't believe it was a lie.
...How about it?
Let's go to the girls' restroom on the third floor right now and try calling Hanako-san out.
{a}{f:|}.
You said earlier that you'd go, didn't you?
Or did hearing my story change your mind?{p}What'll it be?
You're coming, right?
Go to the third-floor girls' restroom
I'm not going after all

I'm so happy.
We really are friends.
No, I already think of you as my best friend.
You've got to solve the mystery of Hanako-san and write a great article.
Then I'll get to be proud, too.
...Even if I end up dead.
Well then, let's go.{p}

...{f:And that was when it happened|Just then}.
"{f:Whoa|Eek}!"
Just as {f:we|we} were about to get up from our seats, we were bathed in a blinding, intense light.
It was dazzling!
What {f:the hell is|is} this light?{p}{f:What the...|No}!
What {f:just happened|is happening}★{p}

We got up from our seats without a word.
When I happened to glance at the classroom clock, it read 10:20.
So was the story from before true after all?
At the very least, that clock had stopped.
Was there a skull-like stain on the back of it?
Maybe my eyes had gotten used to the dark, because I could get around well enough by moonlight alone.
...But if I'd known things would turn out like this, I would have brought a flashlight.
Hosoda and I left the classroom together.{p}
Even though it was summer, the wind felt awfully cold.{p}

Was that because I was scared?
This was the first floor.{p}

We climbed the stairs.
What a horrible sound they made.{p}

It sounded like vengeful spirits laughing at us.
We passed the second floor and kept on climbing the stairs to the third.{p}

Once we reached the top of the stairs and turned the corner, the girls' restroom would be on the left.
We turned the corner, and the girls' restroom we were heading for...{p}

Its light was on.
In the old school building, where no light should ever come on, and in the very girls' restroom where Hanako-san was said to be, the light was on.
"What do we do?
Should we go home after all?"
Hosoda whispered in my ear.
His voice was shrill and hoarse.
He wasn't even touching me, yet I could clearly feel his body trembling.
I couldn't stop myself from shaking, either.{p}

What should I do?
If I was going to turn back, now was the time.
And this was probably my last chance.
What should I do?
Keep going?
Or just go home?{p}
Go to the girls' restroom
Go home now

"Let's go."
When I said that, Hosoda took hold of my hand.
"...You're brave.
I'm scared.
I know it's strange for me to say this when I'm the one who suggested coming...
But I'm so scared I can't stand it."{p}

"Everyone who's told a story so far has disappeared.
Every time a story ends, something bad happens.
...It's my turn now, isn't it?
I'm the one who's going to disappear, aren't I?"{p}

Hosoda's hand was clammy with sweat.
And sweat was pouring from all over his face, glistening slickly.
"Please.
Please don't abandon me."
"I know."{p}
As I stepped forward, I could clearly feel Hosoda's hand tighten around mine.{p}

We stood in front of the girls' restroom.
"...We're going in."
Hosoda gave a small nod at my words.
There was nothing inside the restroom.
Maybe because it hadn't been used in a long time, an indescribable sour stench hung over everything.
...The second stall from the back.
According to the rumor, that was where Hanako-san was.
But the others looked suspicious too.
For now, I stood in front of the second stall from the back.{p}What should I do?
Should I try knocking?
Knock
Don't knock

I was supposed to knock three times, right?
Just as I'd been told earlier, I knocked three times.{p}

Knock... knock... knock...
Would there be an answer...?{p}

Knock... knock... knock...
An answer came back.{p}
There was no doubt about it.
Something was in there!{p}

"Let's stop! That's enough!
Let's go home, {a}!"{p}
Hosoda's face had gone white as a sheet.{p}

"Gyaaaaaah!"
At that moment...{p}

Suddenly, Hosoda's body floated up into the air, and then it was slammed into the ceiling with tremendous force.
As if he were falling up onto the ceiling.{p}

"I-it hurts.
...It hurts... {a}..."
For a moment, I couldn't understand what had happened.
As if only the space around Hosoda had turned into a vacuum, he was writhing in agony on the ceiling.
It looked like some invisible force was pressing him harder and harder against it.
"...Help... me..."
Hosoda groaned in pain, but there was nothing I could do.{p}What should I do?
Try to help him?
Or... run?{p}
Try to help him
Run away from there

I wanted to help him, but I didn't know how.
Even if I stretched out my hand, I couldn't reach the ceiling.
"Uh... uaah..."
While I floundered, not knowing what to do, Hosoda's face slowly began to twist in terror.{p}

The door of the second stall from the back stood open, and a masked girl was standing there.
Suddenly, her voice rang out directly inside my head.
"...Do you want to save him?"
She slowly pointed at Hosoda, pinned to the ceiling.
I nodded.
Then her voice rang out again.
"...Then it will cost your parents' lives.
If you have no parents, I will take the life of the child you will someday have.
Do you accept?"
...The masked girl was forcing the ultimate choice on me.
Save Hosoda, or else my...
You've got to be kidding!{p}

"Help me!
We're friends, aren't we?!
Please!
If you help me, I'll do anything!"
Hosoda was crying, his face all crumpled up.
Could Hosoda hear the voice that had rung out in my head, too?
That voice was pressing me to choose.{p}

"Well?
Will you save him?
Or..."
What should I do?
What am I supposed to do?!{p}
Save Hosoda
Leave Hosoda to die

"...Please save Hosoda."
It wasn't that I'd abandoned my family.
If I could just smooth things over here, I was sure to find a way out.
For now, I had to save Hosoda.
That was what I thought, and I answered on the spot.
It seemed to me that she smiled behind her mask.
"No."{p}

The instant that rang out in my head, Hosoda's body began sinking into the ceiling.
Like someone sinking beneath the surface of water, the ceiling turned soft and squishy for a moment, and Hosoda was swallowed up into it.{p}

"No! I don't want this!
Help me!
Waaaaaaaaaah!"{p}

She just stood there, watching me in silence.
What kind of eyes was she watching me with, behind that mask?
What on earth was going to happen to me...?{p}Finally left all alone, I...

Huh?
That's not like you.
I can't believe that's coming from the person who planned this whole feature.
This is Hanako-san of the restroom we're talking about.
I think she'd be perfect for a seven wonders feature.{p}You're actually interested, aren't you?
Actually, I am
No way, absolutely not
I knew it.{p}

No, you can't!
We're going to call Hanako-san out.
There's a reason we have to.{p}I'll tell you what it is, so please say you're on board.
If that's the case, I'm on board
No means no

Thank you.
Then listen to my story.{p}

I see.
You're more of a coward than I thought.
Fine, then.
We'll go by ourselves.
With that, Hosoda and the others stood up.{p}

I see.
You're more of a coward than I thought.
Fine, then.
I'll go, even if it's just me.
With that, Hosoda stood up.{p}

"I'm really going. Is that all right with you?"
I don't want to be left here alone!
{f:I'm|I'm} coming with you.
...That's what I meant to say.
But my tongue wouldn't move.
{f:It was|It was} as if someone were holding it down.
"...I see. You're stubborn, too."
Hosoda sighed.
That's not it!
I'm telling you, I want to go with you☆
...But no voice came out.
Worse, when I tried to stand up, my body wouldn't even move!
A cold sweat slid down my spine.{p}

What {f:had|had} happened to {f:my|my} body★
{f:My|My} face must have gone white as a sheet just then{f:|}.
But Hosoda turned his back on {f:me|me}.
"If you feel like it, you're welcome to come after me."{p}
It's not Hosoda
It has to be Hosoda

I nearly screamed in terror.
But, again, no voice came out.
It started to feel like I couldn't breathe.
The footsteps grew louder.
Clack... clack... clack...
At last they reached the door.{p}

As if nothing had happened, the footsteps moved away.
That taut clack... faded off down the far end of the hallway{f:.|.}{p}

I was saved.
I didn't know what that thing just now was, but at least it hadn't been after {f:me|me}.
The moment my shoulders slumped in relief, I could suddenly move again.
I tried moving both hands.
Feeling had come back to my tongue, too, which had been like stiff rubber.
{f:I|I} muttered without thinking.
"What {f:the hell was that|was that}...?"
I shook my head lightly and stood up.
Without thinking, I looked behind me.{p}
